messages:
alex_support: Customer ACCT-42 filed an escalation — intermittent 500s + 401s after what looks like a region failover. They say their traffic should be hitting us-west but metrics show spikes to eu-west. billing spike reported. attaching their minimal repro.

lisa_custsuccess: pinging customer for request IDs and the time window, thanks alex :pray:

acme_engineer: here's a minimal repro we ran from our app in us-west:
```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Client-Region: us-west' https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
We get 200 sometimes but ~20% of requests return 401 {"error":"auth_mismatch","details":"token region mismatch"} and other times 500.

maria_sre: can you paste one of the failing response headers + the x-request-id? also which model/route were you using?

acme_engineer: sample response header and trace from last failed request:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Tue, 03 Oct 2023 16:06:21 GMT
x-request-id: req_78f3b2c9
x-eval-region: eu-west-1
x-proxy-node: proxy-12
content-type: application/json

{"error":"auth_mismatch","expected_region":"us-west-2","received_region":"eu-west-1","token_id":"tk_abc123"}
```
route: /v1/generate (default model route)

jon_oncall: looking at infra logs around req_78f3b2c9 — we have a heartbeat flapping event for the us-west probe right before that. deploy-bot shows a failover executed.

deploy-bot: [automated] 2023-10-03T16:06:18Z failover: policy="auto_failover" from_region="us-west-2" to_region="eu-west-1" trigger="healthcheck:us-west-probe (3 consecutive fails)" failover_id="fov_20231003_160618"

jon_oncall: ptal to these probe logs — notice overlapping IP rotation for our healthcheck agents and a NAT gateway churn. timestamps below:
```
2023-10-03T16:06:10Z probe(us-west-probe) INFO send ping -> 10.0.1.22
2023-10-03T16:06:14Z probe(us-west-probe) WARN response 504 from backend
2023-10-03T16:06:15Z probe(us-west-probe) ERROR HEARTBEAT_FAIL code=EPIPE
2023-10-03T16:06:18Z probe(us-west-probe) INFO rotate ip -> 10.0.2.11
2023-10-03T16:06:18Z failover-manager INFO executed failover fov_20231003_160618
```

maria_sre: this looks like a false-positive from the healthcheck stack. probe IP rotation + short backend hiccup triggered threshold. failover moved live traffic to eu-west where the customer's tokens are not valid (they use region-scoped tokens).

alex_support: customer uses region-scoped auth tokens? we need to confirm. acme_engineer?

acme_engineer: correct — our tokens are bound to us-west-2. We saw immediate 401s after the failover and invoices spiked because some retries hit eu-west and ended up on higher egress rates.

lisa_custsuccess: ok confirming root cause hypothesis: false failover -> cross-region routing -> auth mismatch + billing. next steps?

maria_sre: quick mitigations:
1) rollback the failover (if it is still active) — set route back to us-west and mark us-west as healthy for this customer only.
2) increase healthcheck failure threshold from 3 -> 6 for the auto_failover policy while we debug.
3) for customers with region-scoped auth, enable a pinning header so they keep hitting the pinned region during rollback: `X-Redwood-Region-Pref: us-west-2`.

jon_oncall: to reproduce internally: run the probe rotation sequence locally and watch routing table changes. small script:
```bash
# simulate nat rotation + probe flaps
for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -H 'Host: health.us-west.redwood' http://probe-agent.local || echo "fail $i"; sleep 1; done
```
should reproduce the 3-fail window.

acme_engineer: is there a safe way to replay the requests that failed so we don't double-bill? we saw retries that pushed tokens to eu-west and were charged.

maria_sre: we can do a replay for failed request-ids through a read-only replay mechanism that does not count against billing. I'll coordinate with billing. For safety, do not re-send from your app until we confirm rollback.

lisa_custsuccess: i'll ask billing for provisional credit while this is investigated — please provide a list of request IDs and approximate token counts.

jon_oncall: long-term fixes we should consider:
- make healthchecks prefer stable source IPs (reduce rotation during sensitive windows)
- augment auto_failover to check control-plane health + token compatibility for affected tenants before promoting region
- add a short "grace period" where requests are retried to the original region if the token indicates region-scoped auth

maria_sre: opened infra ticket INFRA-9832 with logs + probes dump, tagging netops for NAT churn. changing auto_failover threshold temporarily.

deploy-bot: [automated] 2023-10-03T16:07:30Z update: failover-policy auto_failover threshold set from 3->6 by maria_sre (temporary)

acme_engineer: confirmed i can no longer reproduce 401s after the policy change, requests are sticking to us-west. thanks everyone :relieved:

lisa_custsuccess: i'll follow up with customer for billing IDs and send an incident summary later today. who owns postmortem?

maria_sre: i'll own the postmortem, will include recommended changes and timeline. cc @netops for NAT fix :eyes:

alex_support: great. leaving thread open until postmortem + billing confirmation. thanks all.
